renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: From the south, Kaumārī — mind herself — offers flowers made of thoughts. From the southwest, Vaiṣṇavī — hearing herself — offers flowers made of sounds.
From the west, Vārāhī — skin herself — pleases Bhairava with flowers of touch. From the northwest, Indrāṇī — sight herself — honors him with the choicest shapes.

From the north, Cāmuṇḍā — tongue herself — honors him with all six tastes on the menu. From the northeast, Mahālakṣmī — nose herself — is worshipped with lovely perfumes. The whole circle is complete.

Over it all stands the field-lord — your own self with a name, packed with all thirty-six realities, praised by every school of thought, handing out powers. And the last bow goes to the whole ringing circle itself — quivering, everywhere inside, always close: your own god-ring, hymned as you.

paragraphs.text: South: Kaumārī, mind itself, dropping thought-flowers. Southwest: Vaiṣṇavī, hearing itself, dropping sound-flowers.
West: Vārāhī, skin itself, touch-flowers that delight. Northwest: Indrāṇī, sight itself, choicest-forms on offer.
North: Cāmuṇḍā, tongue itself, six-taste spread. Northeast: Mahālakṣmī, nose itself, perfume game strong. Circle complete.

Top of the stack: field-lord — the self, named, thirty-six realities packed in, six schools co-sign, siddhis on tap. Final bow to the whole buzzing ring — quivering pith, all-inside, never far: your god-circle, hymned as you.
